html:
A Czech priest and teacher at the university of Prague who called for church reform a century before Martin Luther. He was burned for heresy in 1415.

Hus preached in Czech at the Bethlehem Chapel. He took up ideas of the English thinker John Wycliffe: that the Bible stood above the pope, that a sinful priest lost his authority, and that selling indulgences was wrong. The church was then split between rival popes, and his attacks found many listeners in Bohemia.

He went to the Council of Constance under a safe conduct from King Sigismund. The council arrested him, tried him, and burned him when he refused to recant.

His death set Bohemia alight. His followers, the Hussites, beat back five crusades in the Hussite Wars from 1419 to 1434 and won the right to take wine as well as bread at communion. Luther later said he had been a Hussite without knowing it.
sum: A Czech priest and teacher at the university of Prague who called for church reform a century before Martin Luther. He was burned for heresy in 1415.
